messages:
anya: Quick note: the new Python quickstart using httpx async streaming can hang when you break out of the async iterator (ctrl-c) — process stays alive. Repro below.

tom: Minimal repro?

anya: Server: fastapi + sse-starlette, just yields every 0.5s. Client: httpx AsyncClient, async with client.stream(...) as r: async for chunk in r.aiter_bytes(): if condition: break

After break the program often doesn't exit. Adding await r.aclose() in finally fixes it for me, but users will hit this if they copy-paste the naive pattern in quickstart.

rachit: Sounds familiar. Likely httpx leaves background reader tasks alive unless response closed explicitly. Two quick mitigations: 1) update sample to close response in finally; 2) server generator should check request.is_disconnected() to stop producing.

anya: I'll open a samples PR to show the proper pattern + add a 1-paragraph caveat in the quickstart. Can someone file an SDK issue to investigate whether our http client wrapper should auto-cancel readers on iterator exit?

tom: Filing SDK issue now, linking the sample PR when ready. Also adding a unit test that runs quickstart and simulates ctrl-c to catch regressions.

ci-bot: ci: created issue RN-314 and added to backlog (labels: dx, sdk, streaming).

anya: Thanks ":thumbsup:" — marking this as high priority for onboarding flow.
